title: Unit 3 : Session 4 : SLO 1 — Shift-and-Add Unsigned Multiplication
sections: 1. Vocabulary Match-Up (Remembering)
1. Multiplicand → C. The number that is being multiplied
2. Multiplier → D. The number by which you multiply
3. Partial Product → E. Result of multiplying the multiplicand by a single multiplier bit
4. Accumulator → B. Register that holds the intermediate product
5. Shift-Left → F. Moves all bits one position to the left
6. Product → A. The result of the multiplication
2. Step-by-Step Description (Understanding) — correct order
1 → Initialize the Accumulator to all zeros.
2 → If the LSB of the Multiplier is 1, add the Multiplicand to the Accumulator.
3 → Shift the Multiplicand one position to the left.
4 → Shift the Multiplier one position to the right.
(In hardware, steps 2–4 form one cycle repeated for each multiplier bit.)
3. Applying the Concept (Applying): 1101 (13) × 1011 (11) by shift-and-add
Initial: Multiplicand = 0000 1101, Multiplier = 1011, Accumulator = 0000 0000
Iteration 1: LSB = 1 → Add: Accumulator = 0000 1101; then shift → Mcand = 0001 1010, Mplier = 0101
Iteration 2: LSB = 1 → Add shifted multiplicand: 0000 1101 + 0001 1010 = 0010 0111 (Accumulator = 0010 0111); shift → Mcand = 0011 0100, Mplier = 0010
Iteration 3: LSB = 0 → No add; shift → Mcand = 0110 1000, Mplier = 0001
Iteration 4: LSB = 1 → Add shifted multiplicand: 0010 0111 + 0110 1000 = 1000 1111
Final Binary Product: 10001111    Final Decimal Product: 143   (13 × 11 = 143)
4. Error Analysis (Analyzing): 101 × 110
Incorrect step number: Step 3.

Error: in Step 3 the accumulator holds 001010 and the shifted multiplicand is 010100; since the multiplier LSB is 1 the sum must be 001010 + 010100 = 011110. The student wrote 011100 — a binary addition error.
5. Design a Problem (Creating)
Chosen 3-bit multiplicand: 111 (7)    Chosen 3-bit multiplier: 101 (5)
Step 1: LSB = 1 → add → Accumulator = 000111; shift → Mcand = 001110, Mplier = 010
Step 2: LSB = 0 → no add; shift → Mcand = 011100, Mplier = 001
Step 3: LSB = 1 → add → 000111 + 011100 = 100011; shift → done
Final Answer: 100011 (binary) = 35 (decimal)
